fields.title: Flywheel Energy Storage & AC Generation Systems
fields.description:
### Master Flywheel Energy Storage & AC Generation

This course teaches you how to build a soundless, fossil-fuel-free power system using a battery, DC motor, flywheel, and AC generator.

Based on real-world innovation from Lagos, Nigeria, this system provides clean, quiet, and sustainable electricity.

### What You'll Learn
- How flywheels store and release energy
- How to use a DC motor as a generator
- The physics of rotational energy
- How to generate AC power from DC sources
- System assembly, tuning, and maintenance

### Why This Matters
- ✅ No fossil fuels
- ✅ Silent operation
- ✅ Low maintenance
- ✅ Scalable design
- ✅ Made with locally available parts
fields.learning_objectives:
By the end of this course, you will be able to:
1. Explain how flywheel energy storage works
2. Build a motor-generator system
3. Generate AC power from DC batteries
4. Maintain and troubleshoot the system
5. Adapt the design for different power needs

fields.title: Introduction to Flywheel Energy Storage
fields.content:
## Welcome to Flywheel Energy Storage

This course introduces a revolutionary way to generate clean, silent electricity.

### What is a Flywheel?
A flywheel is a mechanical device that stores rotational energy. When you spin it, it stores energy; when you need power, it releases that energy.

### Why Use a Flywheel?
- Stores energy efficiently
- No chemical degradation (unlike batteries)
- Long lifespan (decades)
- Instant power delivery

### The Lagos Innovation
A Nigerian inventor in Lagos created a system using:
- A 12V or 24V DC battery
- A DC motor (acting as generator)
- A heavy flywheel (for energy storage)
- A belt drive system
- An AC alternator

### How It Works
1. Battery powers a DC motor
2. Motor spins a heavy flywheel
3. Flywheel stores rotational energy
4. Flywheel drives an AC alternator
5. Alternator produces AC power
6. System runs silently and continuously

### Preview
In this course, you'll learn:
- Physics of rotational energy
- How to select the right motor and flywheel
- How to connect the system
- How to maintain it

Let's begin!

fields.title: DC Motors as Generators
fields.content:
## DC Motors as Generators

Most people think of motors as devices that consume electricity. But a motor can also *produce* electricity when spun.

### How a DC Motor Works
A DC motor has:
- Rotor (spinning part with coils)
- Stator (stationary magnets or coils)
- Commutator (switches current direction)

### Motor → Generator Mode
When you spin a DC motor, it generates electricity.
- The coils cut through magnetic fields
- This induces a voltage
- The voltage is proportional to speed

### Why Use a DC Motor?
- Readily available and affordable
- Simple to connect
- Works at low speeds
- Can be used with flywheels

### Selecting the Right Motor
- **Voltage**: 12V, 24V, or 48V systems
- **Power**: 500W, 1kW, 2kW, etc.
- **Speed**: High RPM motors produce more power
- **Type**: Permanent magnet motors work best

### Practical Tip
A 1kW DC motor (commonly used in electric scooters) can power a small house when paired with a flywheel and alternator.

### Exercise
Research the DC motors available in your local market. What voltage and power ratings are common?

fields.title: Flywheel Design and Physics
fields.content:
## Flywheel Design and Physics

The flywheel is the heart of this system. It stores energy mechanically.

### Physics of a Flywheel
- **Kinetic Energy**: Energy stored in rotation
- **Formula**: E = ½ I ω²
  - E = energy (joules)
  - I = moment of inertia (depends on mass and shape)
  - ω = angular velocity (speed of rotation)

### Key Principles
1. **Heavier flywheel** = more energy storage
2. **Faster rotation** = more energy (energy scales with speed²)
3. **Larger diameter** = more inertia

### Materials
- **Steel**: Strong, heavy, durable (best for most systems)
- **Cast iron**: Cheap, heavy, easy to machine
- **Composite materials**: Light, strong (expensive)

### Safety First!
Flywheels spin at high speeds and store enormous energy.
- Always use a protective enclosure
- Use quality bearings
- Balance the flywheel properly
- Never exceed rated speeds

### Design Example
- Material: Steel disc
- Diameter: 50cm
- Weight: 25kg
- Speed: 1500 RPM
- Energy storage: ~10kJ

### Exercise
Calculate the stored energy of a 20kg flywheel with a diameter of 40cm spinning at 1200 RPM.

fields.title: AC Power Generation
fields.content:
## AC Power Generation from DC Sources

How do we get AC power from a DC source?

### The System Chain
DC Battery → DC Motor → Flywheel → AC Alternator → AC Power

### Why AC Power?
- Most appliances use AC power
- AC is easier to transmit over distance
- AC can be transformed to different voltages
- AC is the standard for household electricity

### The AC Alternator
An alternator is a device that produces AC power.
- Uses spinning magnets and coils
- Produces alternating current
- Can be a car alternator or a custom generator

### Connecting the System
1. Connect DC battery to DC motor
2. Motor spins the flywheel
3. Flywheel drives the alternator
4. Alternator outputs AC power

### Voltage Regulation
- Use a voltage regulator to maintain stable output
- Inverters can convert DC to AC if needed
- Load matching: ensure the system can handle the load

### Practical Example
- 24V battery → 1kW DC motor
- 25kg flywheel at 1500 RPM
- 5kW AC alternator
- Produces 220V AC at 50Hz (or 120V at 60Hz)

### Exercise
List all the appliances you could power with a 3kW AC system.

fields.title: System Integration and Maintenance
fields.content:
## System Integration and Maintenance

Assembling the system correctly ensures safety, efficiency, and longevity.

### Assembly Steps
1. **Mount the motor**: Secure to a solid base
2. **Mount the flywheel**: Align with motor shaft
3. **Connect the belt**: Use quality v-belts
4. **Mount the alternator**: Align with flywheel
5. **Wire the electrical system**: Use proper gauge wire
6. **Test systematically**: Test each component

### Maintenance Checklist
- **Daily**: Check belt tension
- **Weekly**: Lubricate bearings
- **Monthly**: Check electrical connections
- **Quarterly**: Inspect flywheel for cracks
- **Annually**: Full system review

### Common Issues and Solutions
| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| Low power output | Check battery charge, belt tension |
| Vibration | Balance the flywheel |
| Noise | Check bearings, alignment |
| Overheating | Add cooling, reduce load |
| No AC output | Check alternator, connections |

### Troubleshooting Flow
1. Check battery voltage → 2. Check motor operation → 3. Check flywheel rotation → 4. Check alternator output → 5. Check final output

### Safety Equipment
- Enclosure for flywheel
- Belt guard
- Circuit breakers
- Fire extinguisher
- Emergency shut-off switch

### Environmental Impact
- ✅ Zero emissions
- ✅ Silent operation
- ✅ No fossil fuels
- ✅ Sustainable
- ✅ Locally sourced components

### Exercise
Design a maintenance schedule for your system. Include daily, weekly, and monthly tasks.
